definitions.explanation: Describes rice or food that has just been cooked and is still hot and at its best. Most commonly used for rice.

examples.japanese: {炊|た}き{立|た}てのご{飯|はん}はおいしい。
{炊|た}き{立|た}てのご{飯|はん}に{味噌汁|みそしる}があれば{十分|じゅうぶん}だ。
examples.english: Freshly cooked rice with miso soup is all I need.

examples.japanese: {炊飯器|すいはんき}を{開|あ}けると{炊|た}き{立|た}てのご{飯|はん}のいい{香|かお}りがした。
examples.english: When I opened the rice cooker, the wonderful aroma of freshly cooked rice wafted out.

notes:
FORMATION: {炊|た}き (stem of {炊|た}く, to cook rice) + {立|た}て (suffix meaning 'freshly done'). The suffix ～{立|た}て attaches to the masu-stem of verbs to mean 'just [verb]ed.'

RELATED ～{立|た}て WORDS:
- {焼|や}き{立|た}て: freshly baked
- {揚|あ}げ{立|た}て: freshly fried
- {淹|い}れ{立|た}て: freshly brewed
- {煎|い}り{立|た}て: freshly roasted

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炊|た}き{立|た}てのご{飯|はん}: freshly cooked rice
- {炊|た}き{立|た}てのつやつやした{白米|はくまい}: glossy freshly cooked white rice
